transcript:
This message comes from Odoo, the all-in-one business management software platform.
Whether you're a small or large business, Odoo gives you one flexible platform built to grow with you.
Try today for free at Odoo.com/NPRPodcasts.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
A federal judge has temporarily blocked President Trump's decision banning three media organizations from the White House.
The judge ruled the White House must restore access to CNN, MSNow, and Politico.
The outlet sued, alleging the White House blocked them because President Trump doesn't like their content.
They say that's a clear violation of the First Amendment.
Chinese leader Xi Jinping says the U.S. and China should be partners, not rivals.
Xi's statement comes as he gears up for a day of meetings with President Trump.
NPR's Jennifer Pack reports from Beijing.
President Xi and Trump are expected to touch on thorny issues like Taiwan, rare earth exports and AI guardrails during the summit.
After the two leaders met in Beijing back in May, there are allegations that both sides have not fully lived up to the commitments made.
But cooperation should be the mainstay, and competition kept within limits,
says Xi in a statement published by Chinese state media after he arrived in the U.S.
He says his goal for a great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and Trump's ambition to make America great again can go hand in hand,
and that the two countries can contribute to each other's success.
Jennifer Pack, NPR News, Beijing.
Both Xi and Trump are likely to discuss the war against Iran and Russia's war against Ukraine.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told the U.N. General Assembly yesterday Russia's war is spreading and threatens the world.
NPR's Michelle Kellman reports the Ukrainian leader supports Trump's call for both Russia and Ukraine to stop hitting each other's energy facilities.
In the Russia-Ukraine war, at least, Zelensky's been proposing this kind of energy ceasefire because Trump has been unhappy with Ukraine strikes on Russian oil and gas infrastructure.
But the Ukrainians obviously want the Russians to stop attacking Ukraine's energy grids ahead of another tough winter.
They also want to allow grain to be exported as before.
NPR's Michelle Kellman reporting.
Australia's Prime Minister says an open AI agent hacked into an Australian government health portal last June.
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese says he spoke with open AI's CEO Sam Altman.
Adam Hancock reports from Sydney.
Anthony Albanese said an open AI agent gained unauthorized access to a portal containing non-public data from Australia's universal health scheme, Medicare.
The tech firm has confirmed the hack, revealing that it occurred in June when the AI agent was researching health statistics.
They added that the breach was discovered during a review of "misaligned model activity".
Albanese has called the hack unacceptable and expressed his concerns to open AI boss Sam Altman.
Australian Defense Minister Richard Marles said the impact of the breach was minor.
You're listening to NPR.
Disgraced film executive Harvey Weinstein has been sentenced to 15 years in prison and his retrial on sex crimes in New York.
He was first convicted in 2020, but that was thrown out on appeal.
New York prosecutors have retried him ever since until winning this conviction.
Separately, Weinstein was convicted of rape in California, sentenced there to 16 years in prison, but a court has determined he will be resentenced.
Former tech executive Elizabeth Holmes is set to be released early from federal prison.
NPR's Bobby Allen reports Holmes was given an 11-year sentence in 2022 after a jury convicted her of fraud.
Holmes ran the blood testing startup Theranos that was once the darling of Silicon Valley.
But a jury found she defrauded investors out of hundreds of millions of dollars
by deceiving them that Theranos could revolutionize health care with just a pinprick of blood.
Her prison sentence had been reduced several times. She was scheduled to be released in 2030.
A new notice sent to Holmes, investor victims from the Bureau of Prisons,
shows she is set to be moved to a halfway house next year. It's unclear what led to her partial freedom.
Holmes has been trending online since comedian Nathan Fielder premiered a documentary called
"You Can See Everything," in which Holmes and her family let Fielder live with them
in the weeks before she turned herself in. Bobby Allen, NPR News.
Forecasters have issued a hurricane watch for the Big Island of Hawaii.
Tropical Storm Nolo is expected to become a hurricane, but it's not expected to make landfall.
It's likely to drop more than two feet of rain on some parts of the Big Island. It's NPR.
